intent: Establish a symmetric, moderately wide five-sensor line array on a balanced mid-sized chassis as a baseline. The goal is to get a clean, completed run on the development tracks and to collect integration feedback on sensing resolution and turn authority before tuning any geometry dimension.
learning: Baseline with no race evidence yet. Next iteration, adjust sensor span, sensor size, and wheel track based on rms_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation from the Integrator's runs.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry and no Integrator feedback yet, so this is a baseline built from the contract's ranges rather than from evidence. I chose a five-sensor line array because the controller needs enough samples across the 25 mm tape to estimate lateral offset smoothly, and five is well inside the 3 to 7 limit. Sensors sit 15 mm apart, spanning 60 mm, so the outer sensors can see the tape as the robot drifts before the centre sensors lose it. Sensors are placed 50 mm ahead of the axle so the steering reaction starts before the wheels reach the bend. I used a 12 mm footprint: it is smaller than the 25 mm tape, so readings change clearly as the line crosses it, and it is not so small that noise dominates. Body width 0.12 m gives an off-track limit of max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, which is a reasonable margin for a line follower. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn authority with the 350 PWM-per-turn-unit mapping. Mass 0.8 kg and body length 0.18 m keep yaw inertia moderate, so the robot can change direction without excessive overshoot. Expected result: a completed run on the development tracks at a moderate speed, with rms error well under 0.05 m. If the Integrator reports sluggish turning or early line loss, the next step is to widen the sensor span or reduce mass. I have not yet made any claims about the controller, which the Integrator owns.
